title: Gateway: Rapid weight ingress, conversion, variant verification, and pin publish pipeline
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Deliver an end-to-end gateway that accepts community weights, performs deterministic conversion and lightweight certification, runs variant-aware validation (functional + perf smoke), and publishes a canonical pin + baseline performance profile into the profile catalog. The pipeline must be safe for public OSS weight submissions, minimize manual triage, provide deterministic artifacts for runtime, and surface regressions before model becomes servable.

Scope:
- Ingest: signed manifest + weights upload (S3) with provenance verification and virus/format scans.
- Conversion: deterministic transform to canonical bundle (quantization metadata retained), deterministic hash generation, and reproducible packaging.
- Variant verification: run 3-tier smoke suites: correctness (tokenization parity, sample-generation checks), perf micro-benchmarks (latency P50/P95 on default GPU shape, memory working set), and safety heuristics (basic prompt red-team signals).
- Pin publish: create a canonical pin (artifact hash + metadata) and publish a first-pass performance profile to the public catalog; mark as provisional until full QA.
- Observability: per-artifact telemetry (conversion time, failure mode, perf profile), end-to-end lineage in the catalog, and failure-level dashboards for triage.

Architecture notes and trade-offs:
- We will run conversion in isolated ephemeral containers (K8s jobs) to reduce cross-contamination and allow easy resource tuning. Trade-off: higher cold-start cost but simpler security boundaries.
- Deterministic conversion requires pinning to specific toolchain versions; we will vendor critical conversion transforms and record toolchain hashes in the artifact metadata.
- Perf smoke uses representative short inputs and a warmed KV-cache simulation to estimate per-token throughput. These are heuristics; full production SLOs require dedicated dedicated pods and longer benchmarks — flagged as follow-up.
- For safety checks we rely on cheap heuristics first (prompt-scoring classifiers) and escalate flagged artifacts to manual review. Full safety evaluation is out of scope for this ticket.

Acceptance criteria:
1) A submitter can upload a signed manifest and weights and receive a pipeline run id.
2) Conversion job completes deterministically and produces a canonical bundle with stable hash across two independent runs.
3) Variant verification produces a structured report (pass/warn/fail) and perf metrics (p50/p95 tokens/sec, peak memory) for the canonical config.
4) Successful artifacts result in a new pin in the catalog with performance profile and provenance links.
5) Failures create actionable incident items with logs and suggested fixes.

Rollout plan: staged enablement (internal-only -> beta external -> public). Canary: only allow pins from pipelines that pass the perf smoke and correctness checks for 2 internal models for 72h before enabling full publication.

Operational runbook highlights:
- Retry policy for transient failures (3 attempts) with exponential backoff.
- Auto-quarantine for artifacts failing conversion determinism.
- Alerts on conversion failure rate > 5% over 1h and any deterministic hash mismatch.
comments: 2026-02-10 - Ticket created by Maya Chen: initial scope and acceptance criteria documented; kickoff meeting scheduled.

2026-02-16 - Architecture review: decided on ephemeral K8s conversion jobs and vendoring conversion tools to guarantee deterministic output. Action: Arjun to prototype container image and reproducible build steps (PR #3412).
2026-02-22 - Decision: use SHA256-of-bundle (metadata+bytes) as canonical pin; include toolchain hashes in metadata. Action: add test asserting two independent conversions produce same bundle hash.

2026-02-28 - Implemented perf smoke harness for single-GPU micro-benchmarks. Initial runs against llama-7b-alike model show P50=42ms/token (warm), memory 7.8GB. Bench PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboard/pull/367
2026-03-03 - Security review kickoff: security requested file type whitelisting and AV scans. Added AV step and signed-manifest validation. Security review assigned to Priya Rao.
2026-03-08 - Integration PR opened for conversion orchestrator + dashboard wiring: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboard/pull/389 (seeking design feedback from PM & design).
2026-03-11 - PM feedback (Evan Morales): require a provisional flag when publishing pins so downstream schedulers can opt-in to beta models. Implemented provisional=true field on catalog entries.

2026-03-12 - Smoke run with community weights (test corpus): two sample OSS models ran through pipeline; one quarantined due to tokenizer mismatch; follow-up action ENG-612348 created to improve tokenizer fallback heuristics.
